description: List the phone numbers your workspace rents: each has a numberId, the number (e164), country, what kind of number it is (mobile, local and so on), what it can carry (voice, sms), what it was bought for (type) and is used for now (uses: outbound or load caller ID, callback, survey or inbound), whether it is the default caller ID, its state (ordering, live, releasing, or failed when the carrier failed its order), activation status while ordering, monthly rate and when it was acquired. Also `allowance`: how many numbers the workspace may hold and how many are left, and whether new numbers are included in the workspace's custom agreement (includedInDeal, with its dealRef), in which case no rental or setup fee is charged for them. Takes no parameters. Use when: the user asks which numbers they have, what a number is used for, or why a number is not live yet. Read-only. Needs numbers:read (owner, admin or billing admin); other roles get 403.
name: listNumbers

allowance.description:
How many numbers this workspace may hold. Served alongside the numbers so a
client never has to infer it from the plan — the limit is overridable
per workspace, so "free plan, therefore none" is a rule that is true until
someone grants an exception.

Advisory: `POST /numbers/orders` enforces the limit itself and refuses on
its own. This is what lets a UI say so first, and it is **absent** if the
allowance could not be read — a billing hiccup does not blank the list.

dealRef.description: The agreement's reference. Present only when `includedInDeal` is true.

includedInDeal.description:
True when a number bought now is covered by the workspace's custom
agreement: no monthly rental and no setup fee are charged for it. The
same rule billing applies, so a client can show "included in your
agreement" instead of prices. False for every workspace without such an
agreement, and once the agreement has ended.

remaining.description:
Null when unlimited. Never negative: limits are enforced on purchase
and never retroactively, so a workspace can legitimately sit above one.

used.description: Numbers held, counting ones still being activated.

acquiredAt.description: When the number first became usable. Absent while still ordering.

countryIso2.description: ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 country of the number.

createdAt.description: When the number was first ordered for this workspace.

failedAt.description: When the carrier's failure of the order was found. Present only in state `failed`.

isDefault.description:
The workspace's default caller ID: used when no number with a
matching use is free. At most one per workspace.

monthlyRateUsd.description: What this number is charged at per month, in USD.

numberId.description: Stable identifier for this number. Use it on every other number route.

orderId.description:
The order this number came from, when it came from one. Pass it to
`GET /numbers/orders/{orderId}` to see what a number in `state:
ordering` is still waiting on. Absent for numbers that predate the
buy flow.

phoneNumberType.description:
What the number is, as the carrier classifies it. This determines what it
can carry — in the UK only `mobile` supports both voice and SMS.

requirementsStatus.description:
Present while the number is being activated. The three that matter are
distinct on purpose: `requirement-info-pending` means information has not
been submitted yet, `requirement-info-under-review` means it has and
someone is checking it, and `requirement-info-exception` means something
submitted was rejected and needs correcting.

state.description:
`ordering` means the number is not usable yet — see `requirementsStatus`.
`live` means it is in service. `releasing` means it is being given back.
`failed` means the carrier failed the number's order after it was placed:
it will never be usable, does not count against your allowance and is
not billed (see `failedAt`).

`pooled`, `platform` and `deleted` never appear in this list: pooled and
deleted numbers belong to no workspace, and `platform` numbers are the
service's own shared infrastructure rather than anything a workspace
rents. They are listed in the enum so a client that stores the value
does not have to change when it grows.

type.description:
What the number is used for. `outbound` is a caller ID for tests this
platform places; `inbound` and `callback` are destinations a customer's
system dials; `survey` is a destination a survey campaign is pointed at,
and is the only type requiring SMS.

What the number was **bought** for. What it may be used for now is
`uses`.

uses.description:
What the number is used for now: always one value, set with
`PATCH /numbers/{numberId}`. Starts as `[type]`. `outbound` and `load`
are caller IDs (standard tests, load-test calls); `callback`, `survey`
and `inbound` are destinations.

title: List Phone Numbers
